correctness.rationale: Maximal independent sets are characterized by independence plus domination, which is used in complete labeled graph enumeration at n=1..5 (1+2+8+64+1024 graphs). Independent recomputation finds 90 gaps of (1,2) in exactly two canonical orbits of 60 and 30. The four maximal independent sets of F={a},{b},{c,e},{d,e} have VC=1; e followed by c or a builds depth-2 online tree. In the connected join G_m, maximal sets consist of singleton universal vertex or a Cartesian product of four choices per block, giving 4^m+1 hypotheses. Concatenated online trees give L>=2m, information bound 4^m+1<2^(2m+1) gives L<=2m. VC>=m by selecting e in each block; projection across blocks and absence of all three nonempty traces for any F-pair prove VC<=m, including singleton-support case. Join and union preserve P4-free. Exhaustive n<=5 verification is full finite enumeration, not extrapolated to all cographs.

value.rationale: The earliest-order separation between adaptive and static membership shattering is a natural finite classification. Amplification proves unbounded discrepancy even inside connected P4-free graphs, an unexpectedly restrictive and motivated family of learnable concept classes.

final_claim: For the concept class of inclusion-maximal independent sets in a finite graph, VCdim=Ldim for all graphs of order <=4; at order five the only gaps are two isomorphism types with (VC,L)=(1,2), occurring 60 and 30 times labeled. The unique cograph type F=K2 join (K2 disjoint union K1) amplifies to connected cographs G_m with VC=m and Ldim=2m.
